articles.title: Shelter backs rent control campaign
articles.summary: This comes after the charity's new head suggested she would take a conciliatory tone towards landlords
articles.ai_summary:
- Shelter supports a campaign for rent control, indicating a shift in strategy under its new head.  
- The charity's leadership hints at a more conciliatory approach to landlords amidst the push for regulation.

articles.title: Civil penalty threat to landlords from tomorrow
articles.summary: June 30 is the deadline for landlords to register with this council scheme
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords face civil penalties starting tomorrow if they haven't registered with the council scheme by the June 30 deadline.  
- Compliance is crucial for landlords to avoid potential fines and legal issues.

articles.title: Section 21 “pushed thousands into homelessness” says government
articles.summary: The government claims the former Section 21 possession powers resting with landlords “pushed thousands into homelessness”. The claim comes in a statement about the repeal of the Vagrancy Act today. This ends nearly two centuries of legislation that has criminalised rough sleeping and begging. Labour says the Act pushed vulnerable people away from support, increased […]
articles.ai_summary:
- The UK government asserts that the old Section 21 eviction powers led to thousands ending up homeless, highlighting a significant housing crisis.
- The repeal of the Vagrancy Act, which criminalized rough sleeping and begging for nearly 200 years, has sparked debate on how to better support vulnerable populations.

articles.title: Warning to check landlord licence renewal date
articles.summary: The warning comes from the National Residential Landlords Association
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords urged to verify their licence renewal dates to avoid compliance issues.  
- The National Residential Landlords Association emphasizes the importance of staying up-to-date with licensing requirements.

articles.title: Property investment is now “borderless” says agency
articles.summary: Dwelly now has a presence in Singapore
articles.ai_summary:
- Dwelly expands its global footprint by establishing a presence in Singapore, highlighting the trend of borderless property investment.  
- The agency emphasizes the growing accessibility and opportunity in the international real estate market for investors.

articles.title: Labour councils turn on Sadiq Khan’s housing plans
articles.summary: Khan has revised downwards his affordable homes quota
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour councils are opposing Sadiq Khan's revised housing plans, which include a reduced quota for affordable homes.  
- The backlash highlights rising tensions within the party over housing strategies amid a growing housing crisis.

articles.title: Council to “engage” with landlords over tougher rental enforcement
articles.summary: The council is run jointly by the Greens and Labour
articles.ai_summary:
- The council, a coalition of Greens and Labour, plans to actively engage with landlords regarding stricter rental enforcement measures.  
- This initiative aims to enhance rental compliance and accountability within the housing sector.

articles.title: Labour MP blames landlords’ rents for size of welfare budget
articles.summary: Margaret Mullane is a Labour MP
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour MP Margaret Mullane attributes the growing welfare budget in the UK to high rents charged by landlords.  
- Mullane calls for action to address the impact of rental costs on social support spending.

articles.title: Traitors winner says high rent makes it tough for first time buyers
articles.summary: Winning The Traitors doesn't mean you can afford to buy a home...
articles.ai_summary:
- High rental costs are making it increasingly difficult for first-time buyers, even for those with significant cash prizes, like winners of shows such as The Traitors.  
- Winning money doesn't guarantee homeownership, as rising property prices continue to outpace income levels.

articles.title: Quick buy firm targets landlords quitting rental sector
articles.summary: The initiative follows the Renters Rights Act triggering many landlords to quit
articles.ai_summary:
- A new quick buy service is launching to cater to landlords exiting the rental market due to recent changes from the Renters Rights Act.  
- This initiative aims to streamline the selling process for landlords affected by the shifting dynamics in the rental sector.

articles.title: Landlords to pay £11,713 bill per property to meet EPC rules
articles.summary: This is according to Landlord Trends research from Pegasus Insight
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords face an average cost of £11,713 per property to comply with new Energy Performance Certificate (EPC) regulations.
- The financial burden comes amid growing scrutiny and regulatory changes impacting the rental market, as revealed by Pegasus Insight's Landlord Trends research.

articles.title: Renters Rights Act has no effect so far, claims agent
articles.ai_summary:
- Foxtons reports that the Renters Rights Act has had no tangible impact on the rental market to date.  
- The agency's findings suggest that renters are still facing the same challenges despite legislative changes.

articles.title: Five lettings agency myths blown out of the water – apparently
